In Simon this is the "usual Poincaré inequality for smooth functions" invoked in the proof of Ch. 2, 2.7 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 651–658).

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv). Integrals over a set are Lebesgue (Bochner) integrals of the restricted measure. Under the measure-preserving linear isometry Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp / PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ), so vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded; for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ, Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Let v be C¹ and δ ≥ 0. Write Q := Q_δ, s := 1 − 2δ ≤ 1 and F(x) := ‖Dv(x)‖ ≥ 0, a continuous function.

0. Trivial case and finiteness. If s ≤ 0 then Q = ∅ and both sides are 0. Assume 0 < s ≤ 1. Then vol(Q) = sⁿ, Q is convex, and |x − y| ≤ √n s for x, y ∈ Q (each |x_i − y_i| < s). v and F are continuous, hence bounded on the compact closure of Q; so all integrands below are bounded measurable functions on sets of finite measure, every integral is finite, the iterated Bochner integral on the left equals the iterated Lebesgue integral of the nonnegative function |v(x) − v(y)|, and Tonelli's theorem applies to the nonnegative continuous integrands below.

1. Segment estimate. For x, y ∈ Q, γ(t) := v((1 − t)x + t y) is C¹ on [0, 1] with γ'(t) = Dv((1 − t)x + t y)(y − x). By the fundamental theorem of calculus, |v(y) − v(x)| = |∫_0^1 γ'(t) dt| ≤ ∫_0^1 F((1 − t)x + t y) |y − x| dt ≤ √n s ∫_0^1 F((1 − t)x + t y) dt.

2. Integrating over Q × Q and using Tonelli for (x, y, t) ↦ F((1 − t)x + t y) ≥ 0 on Q × Q × [0, 1]: ∫_Q ∫_Q |v(x) − v(y)| dy dx ≤ √n s ∫_0^1 J(t) dt, where J(t) := ∫_Q ∫_Q F((1 − t)x + t y) dy dx.

3. Bound for t ∈ [1/2, 1]. Fix x ∈ Q. The map y ↦ (1 − t)x + t y is a translate of the dilation by t, whose Jacobian determinant is tⁿ; by the change-of-variables formula for dilations and translations of Lebesgue measure (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.setIntegral_comp_smul_of_pos or MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_comp_smul, together with translation invariance MeasureTheory.integral_add_left_eq_self; all integrands are bounded measurable on bounded sets, so the Bochner versions apply), ∫_Q F((1 − t)x + t y) dy = t^{−n} ∫_{(1 − t)x + tQ} F(z) dz. By convexity, (1 − t)x + tQ ⊆ Q, and F ≥ 0, so this is ≤ t^{−n} ∫_Q F ≤ 2ⁿ ∫_Q F. Integrating over x ∈ Q (measure sⁿ): J(t) ≤ 2ⁿ sⁿ ∫_Q F.

4. Bound for t ∈ [0, 1/2). By Tonelli, J(t) = ∫_Q ∫_Q F((1 − t)x + t y) dx dy. Fix y ∈ Q; the map x ↦ (1 − t)x + t y has Jacobian (1 − t)ⁿ ≥ 2^{−n} and maps Q into Q (convexity); as in step 3, ∫_Q F((1 − t)x + t y) dx ≤ (1 − t)^{−n} ∫_Q F ≤ 2ⁿ ∫_Q F, and integrating over y ∈ Q gives J(t) ≤ 2ⁿ sⁿ ∫_Q F.

5. Conclusion. By steps 2–4, ∫_Q ∫_Q |v(x) − v(y)| dy dx ≤ √n s · 2ⁿ sⁿ ∫_Q F = 2ⁿ √n s^{n+1} ∫_Q ‖Dv‖ ≤ 2ⁿ √n ∫_Q ‖Dv‖, because 0 < s ≤ 1 and ∫_Q ‖Dv‖ ≥ 0. With n = m + 1 this is 2^{m+1} √(m + 1) ∫_{Q_δ} ‖Dv‖. ∎
